title: DCiaB site configuration
description: The single input to DCiaB. Every site-specific field is required and has no default; an optional field's default is the same for every site.

metadata.description: the site's identity; only name is read

name.description: short site id: 2-12 characters, lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, not starting or ending with a hyphen

spec.description: the site: its platform, network, clusters and the services DCiaB builds

bundleVersion.description: the DCiaB archive version this config is written for, as in the archive's VERSION file: the SemVer form of a release name, N.0.0-alpha.M (rNalphaM), N.0.0-beta.M (rNbetaM) or N.0.0 (rN). validate checks they match

platform.description: the hypervisor platform MGMT, INFRA and VM workload clusters run on: vSphere or Proxmox VE, one per site. Read by validate --live, seed, cluster-values and mgmt

kubernetes.description: the Kubernetes version of every cluster

version.description: the Kubernetes version, vX.Y.Z. It must be the one this archive's bundle.lock pins, which its node images and ClusterClasses are built for (validate checks)

bootstrap.description: the bootstrap host (server zero, or a Rocky Linux 10 host you provide): its network, its work disk and the keys that open break-glass material. Read by media, services, seed and every later step

interface.description: the bootstrap host NIC on the node network: its name, or its MAC (quoted) when the name isn't known in advance, as on the DCiaB bootstrap appliance

managementVLAN.description: tagged: the bootstrap NIC tags network.nodes.vlan; untagged: it sits on an access port. Required by the DCiaB bootstrap appliance, which configures its own network

disk.description: the disk, by one or more root device hints

oneOf.description: disk: the local disk the DCiaB appliance installs onto and works from (wiped), selected like rootDeviceHints
path: a directory on a Rocky Linux 10 bootstrap host you provide

workDisk.description: where the bootstrap host keeps the payload dciab media copies from the USB, and its heavy state (container storage, kind, the seed registry)

address.description: the bootstrap host's IPv4 address on the node network. The seed registry (registry.<network.domain>) and the Day 0 services answer on it; validate checks it is inside network.nodes.cidr and that nothing else uses it

recipients.description: at least two age public keys, so break-glass access never depends on one person

network.description: the node network, DNS, storage networks and load balancing that every cluster shares

time.description: where nodes, hypervisors and BMCs get their time (ADR 0010, decision 9)

failureDomains.description: the hardware that fails independently, and how clusters spread across it (ADR 0010)

clusters.description: the two platform clusters, both on platform.type. Workload clusters are in workloadClusters

mgmt.description: MGMT: the self-managing cluster that owns every cluster's machines through Cluster API, built by dciab mgmt. Its lbPool must hold baremetal.ironicIP

infra.description: INFRA: the cluster for platform services (identity, secrets, Git, GitOps, object storage, observability), built by the infra step (planned)

storage.description: block storage (ADR 0008, decisions 4 and 4a): INFRA's provider, and overrides for MGMT and workload clusters. The storage step of dciab mgmt reads it for MGMT

backup.description: backups and disaster recovery (ADR 0009). Leave it out only on a config in the old form: validate then reads the site target from the Longhorn settings' backupTarget and warns, and errors when there is none

pki.description: the platform CA that nodes, the seed registry and platform services trust: generated by seed, or the site's intermediate (ADR 0005)

identity.description: who administers the site and how people log in (ADR 0004; ADR 0008, decision 3; docs/IDENTITY.md)

baremetal.description: bare-metal servers that Metal3 provisions as nodes of metal3 workload clusters (planned). Set enabled: false when the site has none

hypervisors.description: optional: hypervisors that dciab hypervisors installs on bare servers before seed. Leave it out when the hypervisors already exist

workloadClusters.description: optional; clusters created during the platform step. Later clusters are added through Git

ipRange.description: an inclusive IPv4 range such as 10.20.110.20-10.20.110.29

fingerprint.description: a SHA-1 or SHA-256 certificate fingerprint as colon-separated hex pairs, quoted

secretRef.description: a secret reference: {file: <path>} or {env: <VARIABLE>}; secrets are never written inline

file.description: a file that holds the secret: a path relative to the config's folder, or absolute. validate checks it exists and isn't readable by others

env.description: an environment variable that holds the secret when the step runs

clusterName.description: 3-20 characters, lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, starting with a letter

server.description: vCenter's DNS name. CAPV, the vSphere cloud provider (CPI) and the vSphere CSI driver reach vCenter at it

thumbprint.description: the fingerprint of vCenter's TLS certificate. CAPV and validate --live trust vCenter by it

datacenter.description: the vSphere datacenter that holds the compute cluster, datastore, folder and network

cluster.description: the compute cluster that runs MGMT and INFRA VMs; validate --live checks it exists. A failure domain may name its own (failureDomains.domains[].vsphere.computeCluster)

datastore.description: the datastore for node VM disks. A failure domain may name its own

folder.description: an absolute inventory path such as /DC1/vm/dciab

resourcePool.description: the resource pool for node VMs, an absolute inventory path such as /DC1/host/Cluster1/Resources/dciab

network.description: the port group for MGMT and INFRA nodes

template.description: the node VM template, built from DCiaB's node image recipe for this archive's Kubernetes version

clusterModules.description: optional, default true: CAPV cluster modules (DRS VM-VM anti-affinity) keep each group's VMs on separate hosts. Set false only on a site without DRS

credentials.description: the vCenter account that CAPV, the CPI and the vSphere CSI driver use; mgmt puts it in each cluster's <cluster>-vsphere-credentials Secret

username.description: the vCenter user, such as dciab@vsphere.local

password.description: the user's password, a secret reference

url.description: the Proxmox API URL, such as https://pve01.example.net:8006

tlsFingerprint.description: the fingerprint of the Proxmox API's TLS certificate; DCiaB and validate --live trust the API by it. Required, except when url names a host spec.hypervisors installs that is one of nodes: then DCiaB trusts the certificate dciab hypervisors pins on first contact (in the host's install record), and a value given here must match the certificate

nodes.description: the PVE nodes DCiaB may use, at least one. templateNode and every failure domain's proxmox.node must be one of them; validate --live checks each is a node of the cluster

templateNode.description: the node that holds the VM template; CAPMOX clones from it (one of nodes)

templateID.description: the node VM template's ID, 100 or more

storage.description: the Proxmox storage that CAPMOX clones node VM disks onto. On local storage (local-lvm, ZFS) a clone stays on the template's node

bridge.description: the bridge node VMs' NIC attaches to (the node network), such as vmbr0

vlanTag.description: the VLAN tag on node VMs' NIC, 1-4094, for a VLAN-aware bridge. Unset: the NIC is untagged. Optional, except with spec.hypervisors.managementVLAN: tagged, where it must equal network.nodes.vlan

credentials.description: CAPMOX's API token. docs/PROXMOX.md lists the privileges it needs; validate --live checks them

tokenID.description: an API token ID such as dciab@pve!capmox

tokenSecret.description: the token's secret, a secret reference. When url names a host spec.hypervisors installs, dciab hypervisors creates the token and writes its secret to this file (validate reports it as pending until then); on the bootstrap appliance, a file under ./secrets/

templateImport.description: how dciab templates logs in to publish the node template on templateNode. Unset: as root@pam with the root password, only on a host dciab hypervisors installed; any other Proxmox VE needs this block, or a template published by hand (docs/TEMPLATES.md)

credentials.description: an API token of its own, never CAPMOX's, with exactly the privileges docs/PROXMOX.md lists for the node template; validate --live checks them

tokenID.description: an API token ID such as template@pve!dciab

tokenSecret.description: the token's secret, a secret reference

type.description: vsphere or proxmox: the platform MGMT and INFRA run on. Give the matching block (vsphere or proxmox) and not the other

vsphere.description: the vSphere settings: required with type vsphere, not allowed with proxmox

proxmox.description: the Proxmox VE settings: required with type proxmox, not allowed with vsphere

domain.description: the site's DNS domain, served by the seed DNS on Day 0 and by MGMT later. Platform names live under it: registry.<domain> (the site registry), auth.<domain> (Authentik), ironic.<domain> (Metal3 images). Hypervisor host names get it appended

upstreamResolvers.description: upstream DNS servers the seed DNS forwards other names to; an empty list forwards nothing (set isolated: true to say that is intended)

isolated.description: optional, default false. true: the site has no upstream DNS on purpose, and upstreamResolvers is empty. Nodes resolve only network.domain, so everything they pull must come through the seed registry. Without it, an empty upstreamResolvers is a warning

nodes.description: the node network: MGMT and INFRA nodes, the bootstrap host, the DNS service IPs and hypervisor management addresses sit in it

cidr.description: the node network. Every address and range of the VM clusters must be inside it

gateway.description: the node network's default gateway, inside cidr

vlan.description: the node network's VLAN ID, 1-4094. The bootstrap host tags it when bootstrap.managementVLAN is tagged

mtu.description: optional MTU of the node NICs, 1280-9216 (default: the platform's, usually 1500)

storage.description: optional storage networks (iSCSI, NVMe-oF), one per multipath fabric: every VM node of a cluster with storageIPRanges gets one extra NIC per entry; nothing changes when it's absent

dnsServiceIPs.description: exactly two addresses in the node network for the DNS service

loadBalancer.description: how LoadBalancer addresses (each cluster's lbPool) are announced: by BGP to the site's routers, or by L2 (ARP). Cilium LB IPAM, planned

mode.description: bgp: announce addresses to the peers below; l2: answer ARP for them on the node network

bgp.description: the BGP settings: required with mode bgp, not allowed with l2

peers.description: the site routers the clusters peer with, at least one

address.description: the peer's IPv4 address; usually on the node network (validate warns otherwise)

replicas.description: 1, 3 or 5 (an odd number for etcd quorum)

cpu.description: vCPUs per control plane VM, at least 2

memoryGiB.description: memory per control plane VM, in GiB, at least 4

diskGiB.description: the root disk, in GiB, at least 25. It holds the OS, the container images and etcd

dataDiskGiB.description: optional, vSphere only: a second disk, in GiB (at least 10), mounted at /var/lib/longhorn so Longhorn never writes to the root disk etcd uses. Applied only when the cluster's block storage is Longhorn. On Proxmox validate rejects it (CAPMOX can't add a second disk); with no block storage or another provider, validate warns and the machines don't get it

name.description: 2-20 characters, lowercase letters, digits and hyphens

replicas.description: how many worker VMs, 0 or more. Over two or more failure domains the pool becomes one MachineDeployment per domain (<pool>-<domain>), with the replicas split evenly

cpu.description: vCPUs per worker VM, at least 2

memoryGiB.description: memory per worker VM, in GiB, at least 4

diskGiB.description: the root disk, in GiB, at least 25

dataDiskGiB.description: optional, vSphere only: a second disk, in GiB (at least 10), mounted at /var/lib/longhorn so Longhorn never writes to the root disk. Applied only when the cluster's block storage is Longhorn. On Proxmox validate rejects it; with no block storage or another provider, validate warns and the machines don't get it

failureDomains.description: optional: the failure domains this pool uses (default: the cluster's)

apiVIP.description: the Kubernetes API's virtual IP, held by kube-vip on the control plane nodes. In the node network, and used by nothing else

nodeIPRange.description: the addresses CAPI's in-cluster IPAM gives this cluster's nodes, in the node network. It must hold every node plus one spare for rolling updates

lbPool.description: the addresses for this cluster's LoadBalancer Services (Cilium LB IPAM, planned), in the node network and used by nothing else. MGMT's must hold baremetal.ironicIP

podCIDR.description: the pod network, /22 or larger (Cilium gives each node a /24). It must not overlap the site's networks

serviceCIDR.description: the Service network, no larger than /12 (the API server's limit). It must not overlap the site's networks

workerPools.description: a list, which may be empty: then control plane nodes run workloads

failureDomains.description: optional: the failure domains this cluster uses (default: every domain of its platform)

storageIPRanges.description: optional: an address range on each storage network these nodes join, by network.storage name

block.description: INFRA's block storage: the provider and its settings, plus overrides for MGMT and workload clusters (ADR 0008)

longhorn.description: the old form of block: {provider: longhorn, longhorn: {...}}, accepted for one minor release. It describes INFRA; MGMT gets no block storage from it (ADR 0008, decision 4a)

storage.description: give block (ADR 0008); longhorn alone is the old form, accepted for one minor release. Not both

blockProvider.description: longhorn, vsphere-csi, proxmox-csi, ceph-csi, vendor-csi or existing (ADR 0008, decision 4). DCiaB installs longhorn, vsphere-csi and proxmox-csi, and uses existing; ceph-csi and vendor-csi are accepted but not installed yet

provider.description: required, no default: INFRA's block storage provider. Usually vsphere-csi on vSphere, proxmox-csi on Proxmox, longhorn on bare metal (Metal3)

longhorn.description: Longhorn's settings: required with provider longhorn, not allowed with the others

vsphereCSI.description: the vSphere CSI driver's settings: optional with provider vsphere-csi, not allowed with the others

proxmoxCSI.description: the Proxmox CSI plugin's settings: required with provider proxmox-csi, not allowed with the others

cephCSI.description: ceph-csi's settings: required with provider ceph-csi, not allowed with the others. Not installed yet: validate says so

vendorCSI.description: the vendor driver's settings: required with provider vendor-csi, not allowed with the others. Not installed yet: validate says so

existing.description: the StorageClass to use: required with provider existing, not allowed with the others

mgmt.description: optional: block storage for MGMT, complete on its own. Without it, MGMT keeps no volumes (ADR 0008, decision 4a)

infra.description: optional: merged over block for INFRA

workload.description: optional: block storage for every workload cluster, complete on its own. Without it, tenants bring their own

overrides.description: optional, per tier: infra, merged over block; mgmt and workload (every workload cluster), which stand alone. Overrides for one cluster come after r1

then.description: with provider longhorn, keep only its longhorn block and remove the others
with provider vsphere-csi, keep only its vsphereCSI block and remove the others
with provider proxmox-csi, keep only its proxmoxCSI block and remove the others
with provider ceph-csi, keep only its cephCSI block and remove the others
with provider vendor-csi, keep only its vendorCSI block and remove the others
with provider existing, keep only its existing block and remove the others

blockStorage.description: INFRA's block storage: the provider and its settings (ADR 0008, decisions 1, 4 and 4a). MGMT and workload clusters don't inherit it

workloadBlock.description: optional: block storage for every workload cluster, a provider and its settings, as under block but with no overrides. Nothing comes from block: without it, DCiaB imposes no block storage on workload clusters and tenants bring their own

mgmtBlock.description: optional: block storage for MGMT, a provider and its settings, as under block but with no overrides. Nothing comes from block: without it, MGMT keeps no volumes and gets no StorageClass (ADR 0008, decision 4a)

provider.description: optional: a provider other than block's; then give its settings block too

vsphereCSI.description: the vSphere CSI driver's settings, complete

proxmoxCSI.description: the Proxmox CSI plugin's settings, complete

then.description: with provider longhorn, keep only its longhorn block and remove the others
with provider vsphere-csi, keep only its vsphereCSI block and remove the others
with provider proxmox-csi, keep only its proxmoxCSI block and remove the others
with provider ceph-csi, keep only its cephCSI block and remove the others
with provider vendor-csi, keep only its vendorCSI block and remove the others
with provider existing, keep only its existing block and remove the others

blockOverride.description: merged over block for INFRA: a provider and its settings block, or a settings block for block's provider. A settings block is complete, as under block

credentials.description: S3 only: KEY=VALUE lines with AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID and AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY

caBundle.description: S3 only, optional: the private CA that signed the endpoint's certificate, in PEM

mode.description: copy: to S3 or NFS at another location; site-replicated: the site target already replicates off site; removable: media the site carries away; none: no off-site copy, with a reason

url.description: copy: the off-site target, s3://<bucket>@<endpoint>[/<path>] or nfs://<server>:/<export>

credentials.description: copy, S3: credentials that can write but not delete

readCredentials.description: copy, S3, optional: read-only credentials for restores

caBundle.description: copy, S3, optional: the private CA that signed the off-site endpoint's certificate, in PEM

retentionDays.description: what the off-site store keeps, in days; default 90

everyDays.description: removable: how often to export, in days; default 7

reason.description: none: why this site has no off-site copy

then.description: with mode copy, give url (and credentials for S3); everyDays and reason belong to other modes
with mode site-replicated, the site target's own replication is the copy: give no url, credentials, everyDays or reason
with mode removable, give at most everyDays (and retentionDays): no url, credentials or reason
with mode none, give a reason, and nothing else

daily.description: the newest of each day, for N days

days.description: every copy of the last N days

backupKeep.description: what the site target keeps; the job prunes by these, never by bucket lifecycle rules. A copy any rule keeps is kept

cronSchedule.description: a five-field cron schedule, in UTC

cron.description: when the job runs: five cron fields, in UTC
when the job runs: five cron fields, in UTC

targets.description: where backups go: the site target and the off-site copy

site.description: required: the site's own S3 bucket or NFS export, outside DCiaB's clusters. MGMT always backs up here

offsite.description: required: the copy that survives losing the site, or mode: none with a reason

target.description: site, always: MGMT never backs up to INFRA (validate rejects anything else)
objectStore (the default: INFRA's object store, SeaweedFS by default; spec.storage.object is planned) or site
objectStore (the default: INFRA's object store; spec.storage.object is planned) or site

etcdSnapshots.description: default true: every workload cluster's etcd is snapshotted

volumeBackups.description: default false: tenants opt volumes in; true backs up every volume of the replicated classes

tiers.description: where each tier backs up (ADR 0009, decision 1). Defaults: mgmt site, infra objectStore, workloads objectStore

publicKey.description: the backup key's age public key

key.description: optional: the backup key's public half (ADR 0009, decision 10). Without it, DCiaB generates one and seals its private half to spec.bootstrap.recipients

capiExport.description: the export of MGMT's Cluster API objects

longhorn.description: Longhorn's recurring jobs, on every cluster that runs Longhorn

snapshot.description: Longhorn snapshots, kept on the volume

backup.description: Longhorn backups to the tier's target

schedules.description: optional: DCiaB's defaults (ADR 0009) apply to anything not given

backup.description: backups (ADR 0009): the site and off-site targets, where each tier backs up, schedules and retention

replicaCount.description: the replicas of each volume in the replicated classes, 1-3. Each needs a node of its own: validate warns when the cluster has fewer nodes that hold Longhorn data, at 1, and when the datastore under it may replicate already (use the array's CSI driver there)

backupTarget.description: the old place of the site's backup target, read only when spec.backup is absent (ADR 0009): s3://bucket@endpoint/path or nfs://server:/export

backupCredentials.description: the old place of the S3 target's credentials (KEY=VALUE lines with AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID and AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY), read only when spec.backup is absent

storagePolicy.description: optional: the vSphere storage policy (SPBM) the StorageClasses name

datastoreURL.description: optional: the datastore URL (ds:///vmfs/volumes/<id>/) the StorageClasses name

vsphereCSI.description: optional; give storagePolicy or datastoreURL, not both. With neither, vCenter picks a datastore every node can reach

storage.description: the Proxmox storage that holds the volumes (any storage that holds VM disks)

shared.description: required, no default: true when the storage is shared in Proxmox (every node reaches it: Ceph RBD, NFS, LVM on a shared LUN), false when it is node-local (local LVM, ZFS, a directory). Storage names don't say which; validate --live checks it against the storage's shared flag

credentials.description: the Proxmox CSI plugin's API token

tokenID.description: an API token of its own, not CAPMOX's, such as csi@pve!dciab (docs/PROXMOX.md)

tokenSecret.description: the token's secret, a secret reference

userID.description: the Ceph client name without client., such as kubernetes

key.description: the Ceph client's key, a secret reference

driver.description: a vendor CSI driver pinned in bundle.lock

storageClass.description: a StorageClass the cluster already has; DCiaB copies it into its four classes

mode.description: generate-root: seed creates the platform root CA, its key stored only encrypted to bootstrap.recipients. import-intermediate: the site's intermediate CA, from certificate, key and chain

commonName.description: generate-root: the common name of the root CA seed creates, such as Example Platform CA. import-intermediate: not used

certificate.description: import-intermediate: the site's intermediate CA certificate, in PEM. validate checks it is a CA that can sign CAs, and that its path length allows the 3 CAs DCiaB puts below it

key.description: import-intermediate: the intermediate's private key, in PEM. It is never copied into the state

chain.description: import-intermediate: the chain from the intermediate up to the site's root, in PEM. It becomes the trust bundle nodes and the bootstrap cluster trust

adminGroup.description: the group whose members administer the platform: cluster-admin on every cluster that trusts an issuer, and admin of Authentik and the platform services. On Kubernetes it carries the issuer's prefix (<name>:adminGroup). With provider external it must be in the site IdP's groups claim

initialAdmins.description: the first administrators, at least one. With authentik, each becomes an Authentik user in adminGroup. Every admin's SSH key goes onto every node (user dciab) and onto the hypervisors DCiaB installs

email.description: the admin's email address, for their Authentik user

provider.description: authentik (default): DCiaB's Authentik on INFRA; external: the site's own OIDC issuer, with no Authentik (ADR 0008, decision 3)

operator.description: optional: the group that gets the operator role (edit on Kubernetes)

viewer.description: optional: the group that gets the viewer role (view on Kubernetes)

roles.description: optional groups for the operator and viewer platform roles; admin is always adminGroup

consumers.description: what logs in through the identity provider. Default: every platform service, not the hypervisors; add proxmox or vcenter to let DCiaB change the hypervisors' identity source

kubernetes.description: optional: JWT issuers the Kubernetes APIs trust in addition to the provider's

issuers.description: JWT issuers the Kubernetes APIs trust in addition to the provider's, for example the site's IdP while people move to it

external.description: the site's OIDC issuer: required with provider external, not allowed with authentik

name.description: the issuer's short name, the prefix of its users and groups on Kubernetes (<name>:). Default: site

claims.description: the ID token claims that hold the user name and groups

caBundle.description: optional: the CA of the issuer's TLS certificate (PEM), when the platform CA doesn't cover it

clientID.description: the client ID the site's IdP gave this consumer

clientSecret.description: the client's secret, a secret reference. Every client except kubernetes, which is public, needs one

clients.description: one client per OIDC consumer, created by the site's IdP team: its client ID and, except for the public kubernetes client, a secret reference

bindDN.description: the DN DCiaB binds as, read-only

ldap.description: optional: the site's directory, for SSSD on hosts (openvox) and vCenter's identity source

vcenterFederation.description: true: the site federates vCenter to its IdP itself, so vcenter in consumers needs no ldap

issuerName.description: 1-62 lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, not system: the name is the prefix of the issuer's users and groups (<name>:), and system: is Kubernetes' own (system:masters bypasses RBAC)

username.description: the claim that holds the user name, such as preferred_username

groups.description: the claim that holds the groups

name.description: short name, the prefix of its users and groups on Kubernetes (<name>:)

url.description: the issuer URL, https, exactly as its tokens' iss claim gives it

clientID.description: the audience its ID tokens carry

caBundle.description: optional: the CA of the issuer's TLS certificate (PEM)

tiers.description: which clusters' APIs trust it. Default: every tier, or only workload clusters for DCiaB's Authentik (auth.<network.domain>), which MGMT and INFRA never trust

name.description: the host's name, a DNS label, unique; its BareMetalHost is named after it

bootMACAddress.description: the MAC address of the NIC the host boots from

rootDeviceHints.description: the disk the OS image is written to

labels.description: labels on the host, at least one. Metal3 clusters' hostSelectors pick hosts by them

failureDomain.description: the name of a spec.failureDomains.domains entry: the host's rack, room or power feed

enabled.description: true: the site has bare-metal servers for Metal3, and every other baremetal field is required. false: give no other field

bootMode.description: UEFI or UEFISecureBoot: how Metal3 boots the hosts

ironicIP.description: Ironic's fixed LoadBalancer address on MGMT, inside clusters.mgmt.lbPool. Hosts fetch OS images from https://ironic.<network.domain>/images/

bmcNetworks.description: the networks the BMCs are on, at least one; MGMT must reach them. validate checks they don't overlap the site's other networks

images.description: the OS images Metal3 writes to hosts, from the archive's os-images/, at least one

name.description: the image's name, which control planes and worker pools name

file.description: a path under os-images/ in the archive

networks.description: the networks Metal3 nodes are on, at least one

gateway.description: the network's default gateway, inside cidr

hosts.description: the servers Metal3 provisions, at least one

else.description: with enabled: false, remove every other baremetal field

replicas.description: 1, 3 or 5 (an odd number for etcd quorum)

network.description: the name of a spec.baremetal.networks entry

nodeIPRange.description: the addresses for these nodes, inside the named network

image.description: the name of a spec.baremetal.images entry

hostSelector.description: labels a host must carry, every one of them, to be chosen

name.description: 2-20 characters, lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, unique in the cluster

replicas.description: how many hosts, 0 or more. Over two or more failure domains the pool is split per domain, as on VMs

network.description: the name of a spec.baremetal.networks entry

nodeIPRange.description: the addresses for these nodes, inside the named network

image.description: the name of a spec.baremetal.images entry

hostSelector.description: labels a host must carry, every one of them, to be chosen

failureDomains.description: optional: the failure domains this pool uses (default: the cluster's)

name.description: the cluster's name: unique, and not mgmt or infra

class.description: vsphere, proxmox or metal3: the ClusterClass, one provider per cluster

apiVIP.description: the Kubernetes API's virtual IP, on the control plane's network

lbPool.description: the addresses for this cluster's LoadBalancer Services, on the control plane's network

serviceCIDR.description: the Service network, no larger than /12

workerPools.description: a list, which may be empty: then control plane nodes run workloads

failureDomains.description: optional: the failure domains this cluster uses (default: every domain that has hosts)

apiVIP.description: the Kubernetes API's virtual IP, in the node network

nodeIPRange.description: the addresses for this cluster's nodes, in the node network

lbPool.description: the addresses for this cluster's LoadBalancer Services, in the node network

workerPools.description: a list, which may be empty: then control plane nodes run workloads

deviceName.description: a disk such as /dev/sda. For a Proxmox VE install (dciab hypervisors) it can't be combined with other hints

model.description: the disk's model, or a part of it

vendor.description: the disk's vendor, or a part of it

hctl.description: the SCSI address, host:channel:target:lun. Not for a Proxmox VE install (dciab hypervisors), whose installer can't match it

minSizeGigabytes.description: the smallest size to accept, in GB. Not for a Proxmox VE install (dciab hypervisors)

rotational.description: true for a spinning disk, false for an SSD or NVMe. Not for a Proxmox VE install (dciab hypervisors)

servedBy.description: dciab: DCiaB serves time on the node-facing addresses (the bootstrap host on Day 0, the platform after); for now it needs spec.hypervisors, whose dciab services runs the Day 0 NTP. site: the site's own NTP servers

upstream.description: servedBy dciab: the NTP servers DCiaB syncs from; an explicit empty list means none (an isolated site)

serveLocalClock.description: servedBy dciab: true only with no upstream; DCiaB's own clock is then the site's time

servers.description: what nodes, hypervisors and BMCs use. servedBy site: the site's NTP servers (required). servedBy dciab: optional, the DNS service addresses (network.dnsServiceIPs), where DCiaB serves NTP

serveLocalClock.description: true: with no upstream, DCiaB's clock is the only time source

upstream.description: empty: serveLocalClock is only for a site with no upstream

time.description: where the site's time comes from (ADR 0010, decision 9)

domains.description: the site's failure domains: hardware that fails independently (a host, rack, room or power feed). Every cluster uses all of them unless it narrows the list

reason.description: why this site runs with fewer than three failure domains, and how it recovers (for example: one server at an edge site; restore is from backups)

notHighlyAvailable.description: required with fewer than three domains: the site isn't highly available, and says so

name.description: 1-20 characters, lowercase letters, digits and hyphens; the value of topology.kubernetes.io/zone on its nodes

proxmox.description: a Proxmox VE domain: one PVE node

node.description: the PVE node in this domain; the domain is named after it

vsphere.description: a vSphere domain: a compute cluster, or a host group within one

computeCluster.description: the compute cluster of this domain

hostGroup.description: a DRS host group, when several domains share one compute cluster

vmGroup.description: the DRS VM group that goes with hostGroup

domainList.description: optional: the spec.failureDomains names this cluster or pool uses (default: all of them)

name.description: 1-15 characters, lowercase letters, digits and hyphens

vlan.description: proxmox: the VLAN tag on the storage NIC

mtu.description: optional MTU of the storage NIC, 1280-9216, often 9000 (default: the platform's)

portGroup.description: vsphere: the port group (required on vSphere)

storageNetwork.description: a storage network: no gateway, so storage traffic stays on its segment

storageIPRanges.description: optional: an address range per network.storage entry (by name) for this cluster's nodes; the nodes get a NIC on each listed network

name.description: the host name, without the domain (network.domain is added)

address.description: the host's management address, in the node network and used by nothing else

bmc.description: the host's BMC, which dciab hypervisors drives over Redfish

bootMACAddress.description: the MAC address of the management NIC

rootDeviceHints.description: the disk the hypervisor is installed on

type.description: proxmox (Proxmox VE, built in part) or esxi (planned)

bootMode.description: UEFI or UEFISecureBoot: the boot mode each server should use. Setting it over Redfish before installing is planned (docs/HYPERVISORS.md)

method.description: virtualmedia: the installer ISO is attached through each host's BMC (Redfish)

installerFile.description: esxi only: path to the ESXi installer ISO, which DCiaB doesn't ship; its sha256 must match bundle.lock

rootPassword.description: optional: the root password for every host DCiaB installs. Unset: DCiaB generates one per host and stores it encrypted to spec.bootstrap.recipients. Either way people log in with the identity.initialAdmins SSH keys

managementVLAN.description: tagged: the management NIC tags network.nodes.vlan on a trunk port (a first-boot hook on the installer ISO sets it); network.nodes.vlan must not be 1 (a bridge's default PVID), platform.proxmox.bridge must be vmbr0 and platform.proxmox.vlanTag must equal network.nodes.vlan; bridgeVids may narrow the VLANs vmbr0 carries. untagged: an access port for network.nodes.vlan, or a trunk with it as the native VLAN (docs/HYPERVISORS.md)

bridgeVids.description: optional: the VLANs a VLAN-aware vmbr0 carries on the hosts DCiaB installs, as Proxmox VE writes bridge-vids: IDs and ranges separated by spaces, such as 2-4094 (the default) or "110 200-210", each within 2-4094. Narrow it for NICs whose VLAN filter table is smaller than 4093 entries. With managementVLAN: tagged it must include network.nodes.vlan and platform.proxmox.vlanTag

keyboard.description: the installed system's keyboard layout, as the Proxmox VE installer names it (e.g. en-us, de, fr-ch)

installer.description: proxmox: locale settings the Proxmox VE installer requires

hosts.description: the servers to install, at least one

hypervisors.description: optional; hypervisors DCiaB installs on bare servers before the seed step. Leave it out when the hypervisors already exist
